decision_conditions: Floodlighting - Hours of UseThe floodlighting hereby approved shall only be used between the hours of 06.30-22.00 Monday to Saturday and 07.30-18.30 Sundays and Bank Holidays.  Reason: To accord with the terms of this application, safeguard the amenities of the area and the occupiers of neighbouring properties and nature conservation in compliance with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: D12.2, D12.3, O15.3 of Merton Local Plan 2024

Lighting Post Installation AssessmentThe external lighting shall be positioned and angled in accordance with the submitted scheme and compliant with the Institute of Lighting Professionals Guidance Note GN01/21 - The Reduction of Obtrusive Light, to prevent any light spillage or glare beyond the site boundary and not exceed Environmental Zone 3 at all nearby residential properties.  A post installation lighting assessment shall be conducted to demonstrate compliance, in particular at the residential facades, and the report submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval. The installation shall be maintained in accordance with that scheme. Reason: To accord with the terms of this application, safeguard the amenities of the area and the occupiers of neighbouring properties in compliance with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: D12.2 and D12.3 of Merton Local Plan 2024.

Lighting IntensityLight intrusion into windows serving residential properties and luminous intensity (glare) shall not exceed an Environmental Zone E3, which is a suburban area with medium district brightness as recommended within The Institution of Lighting Professionals: Guidance Notes for The Reduction of Obtrusive Light GN01:2021, or equivalent. Reason: To accord with the terms of this application, safeguard the amenities of the area and the occupiers of neighbouring properties in compliance with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: D12.2 and D12.3 of Merton Local Plan 2024.

Boundary and Elevational DetailsPrior to first use of the development hereby approved, details of all new boundary elevational details associated with the development hereby approved shall be submitted and be approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To safeguard the visual amenities of the area and the occupiers of neighbouring properties in compliance with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: D12.2 and D12.3 of Merton Local Plan 2024.

<p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;"><u>NMP</u></span></p><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">No use of the development hereby permitted shall commence until a detailed Noise Management Plan (NMP) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The NMP shall set out the measures to control and mitigate noise arising from the operation of the site and shall include, but not be limited to:</span></p><ul role="list"><li><p><span role="button" tabindex="0" data-url="ca://s?q=Define_hours_of_operation_for_noise_control" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Hours of operation </span><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">specifying permitted hours for all noise‑generating activities.</span></p></li><li><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;"><span role="button" tabindex="0" data-url="ca://s?q=Outline_noise_management_procedures">Management procedures</span> including staff training, supervision, and protocols for managing noisy behaviour.</span></p></li><li><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;"><span role="button" tabindex="0" data-url="ca://s?q=Explain_noise_monitoring_and_review_processes">Monitoring and review</span> detailing how noise levels will be monitored, recorded and reviewed.</span></p></li><li><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;"><span role="button" tabindex="0" data-url="ca://s?q=Detail_noise_complaints_procedure">Complaints procedure</span> including response times and reporting to the Local Planning Authority.</span></p></li></ul><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">The approved Noise Management Plan shall be implemented in full for the lifetime of the development unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.</span></p><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Reason: To protect the amenities of neighbouring occupiers in accordance with Policy D12.3 of the Merton Local Plan, Policy D14 of the London Plan and the aims of the NPPF.</span></p>

<p><span style="white-space-collapse: preserve;">Community Use Agreement</span></p><p><span style="white-space-collapse: preserve;">Prior to fist use of the development hereby approved a community use agreement prepared in consultation with Sport England shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, and a copy of the completed approved agreement shall be provided to the Local Planning Authority. The agreement shall apply to the development hereby approved and include details of pricing policy, hours of use, access by non-educational establishment users /non-members, management responsibilities and a mechanism for review. The development shall not be used otherwise than in strict compliance with the approved agreement."
</span></p><p><span style="white-space-collapse: preserve;">Reason: To secure well managed safe community access to the sports facility/facilities, to ensure sufficient benefit to the development of sport and to accord with Development Plan Policy</span></p>

<p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;"><u>Drainage Strategy</u></span></p><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">No development shall commence (excluding site clearance and enabling works) until a detailed Drainage Strategy has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The strategy shall be based on sustainable drainage principles and shall include:</span></p><ul role="list"><li><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Full details of all SuDS components, including permeable surfacing, sub‑base attenuation, filter drains, silt traps, flow‑control devices and grey‑water harvesting systems</span></p></li><li><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Confirmation of the proposed connection points, discharge rates and capacity within the receiving network</span></p></li><li><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Evidence of consultation with Thames Water, including any required build‑over agreements</span></p></li><li><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">A plan demonstrating maintenance access to attenuation tanks and flow‑control chambers</span></p></li><li><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">A long‑term management and maintenance plan, including responsibilities, access arrangements and inspection frequencies</span></p></li></ul><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">The approved Drainage Strategy shall be implemented in full prior to first use of the development and shall thereafter be retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development.</span></p><p><div></div></p><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;"><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Reason:</span> To ensure the development incorporates an appropriate and sustainable drainage system, manages surface‑water runoff effectively, and does not increase flood risk on‑ or off‑site, in accordance with London Plan Policy SI 13 and Local Plan Policy F15.8 and F15.9,</span></p>

Commencement of development (Full Permission) - The development to which this permission relates shall be commenced not later than the expiration of 3 years from the date of this permission.

Reason:  To comply with Section 91 (as amended) of the Town & Country Planning Act 1990.

Security - The development hereby permitted shall incorporate security measures to minimise the risk of crime and to meet the specific security needs of the development in accordance with Secured by Design. Details of these measures shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority prior to commencement of the development and shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details prior to occupation.

Reason: In order to achieve the principles and objectives of Secured by Design to improve community safety and crime prevention in accordance with Section 17 Crime and Disorder Act 1988, the National Planning Policy Framework, Policy D11 of the London Plan and policies D12.1, D12.2 and D12.3 of the Local Plan 2024.

External Materials as Specified - The facing materials to be used for the development hereby permitted shall be those specified in the application form unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

Reason:  To ensure a satisfactory appearance of the development and to comply with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policies D4 and D8 of the London Plan 2021, policies D12.1 and D12.3 of the Local Plan 2024.

Security - Prior to occupation a Secured by Design final certificate or its equivalent from the South West Designing Out Crime office shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: In order to achieve the principles and objectives of Secured by Design to provide a safer environment for future residents and visitors to the site and reduce the fear of crime in accordance with Section 17 Crime and Disorder Act 1988, the National Planning Policy Framework, Policy D11 of the London Plan and policies D12.1, D12.2 and D12.3 of the Local Plan 2024.

Refuse stored - No refuse or waste material of any description shall be left or stored anywhere on the site other than within a building or refuse enclosure.

Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the property and the amenities of the area and to accord with Policies D3 and D6 of the London Plan 2021and policy D12.3 of the Local Plan 2024.

Restriction on Music/Amplified Sound - No music or other amplified sound generated on the premises shall be audible at the boundary of any adjacent residential building.

Reason:  To safeguard the amenities of surrounding area and to ensure compliance with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policies D4 and D14 of the London Plan 2021 and policies D12.1 & D12.3 of the Local Plan 2024.

﻿No External Lighting - No external lighting shall be installed without the prior approval in writing of the Local Planning Authority.

Reason:  To safeguard the amenities of the area and the occupiers of neighbouring properties and ensure compliance with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policies D12.1 & D12.3 of the Local Plan 2024.

Construction Times (Major Development) - No demolition or construction work shall take place before 8am or after 6pm Mondays - Fridays inclusive, before 8am or after 1pm on Saturdays or at any time on Sundays or Bank Holidays.

Reason:  To safeguard the amenities of the area and the occupiers of neighbouring properties and ensure compliance with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policies D14 and T7 of the London Plan 2021 and policies D12.1 & D12.3 of the Local Plan 2024.

Air Quality - All Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) of net power of 37kW and up to and including 560kW used during the course of the demolition, site preparation and construction phases shall comply with the emission standards set out in chapter 7 of the GLA's supplementary planning guidance "Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition" dated July 2014 (SPG), or subsequent guidance.

Unless it complies with the standards set out in the SPG, no NRMM shall be on site, at any time, whether in use or not, without the prior written consent of the local planning authority. The developer shall keep an up to date list of all NRMM used during the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development on the online register at https://nrmm.London/

Reason: To comply with Policy SI1 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy P15.10 of the Local Plan 2024.

Construction Vehicles - The development shall not commence until details of the provision to accommodate all site workers', visitors' and construction vehicles and loading /unloading arrangements during the construction process have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.  The approved details must be implemented and complied with for the duration of the construction process.

Reason: To ensure the safety of pedestrians and vehicles and the amenities of the surrounding area and to comply with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policies T4 and T7 of the London Plan 2021 and policies T16.3 and T16.4 of the Local Plan 2024.

Provision of turning head - The coach/vehicle turning head shown on drawings hereby approved shall be kept clear from any obstruction / parked vehicles at all times.  

Reason: To safeguard the free flow of traffic in the surrounding and comply with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policy T6 of the London Plan 2021 and policy T16.4 of the Local Plan 2024

Unexpected Contamination - If during construction works any contamination is encountered which has not previously been identified and considered the Council's Environmental Health Section shall be notified immediately and no further development shall take place until remediation proposals (detailing all investigative works and sampling, together with the results of analysis, risk assessment to any receptors and proposed remediation strategy detailing proposals for remediation) have been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority and the approved remediation measures/treatments implemented in full.

Reason: In order to protect the health of future occupiers of the site and adjoining areas in accordance with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policy SI 10 of the London Plan 2021 2021 and policy D12.1 of the Local Plan 2024.

Sustainable Drainage - No development approved by this permission shall be commenced until a scheme for the provision of surface water drainage has been implemented in accordance with details that have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Before these details are submitted an assessment shall be carried out of the potential for disposing of surface water by means of a sustainable drainage system (SuDS) to ground, watercourse or sewer in accordance with drainage hierarchy contained within the London Plan Policy 5.13 and the advice contained within the National SuDS Standards. Where a sustainable drainage scheme is to be provided, the submitted details shall:

   i. provide information about the design storm period and intensity, the method employed to delay (attenuate) and control the rate of surface water discharged from the site as close to greenfield runoff rates (8l/s/ha) as reasonably practicable and the measures taken to prevent pollution of the receiving groundwater and/or surface waters;

   ii.  include a timetable for its implementation; and

   iii. provide a management and maintenance plan for the lifetime of the development which shall include the arrangements for adoption by a public authority or statutory undertaker and any other arrangements to secure the operation of the scheme throughout its lifetime.

Reason: To ensure satisfactory means of surface water drainage, to reduce the risk of flooding and to comply with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policy SI 13 of the London Plan 2021 and policies F15.7, F15.8 and F15.9 of the Local Plan 2024.

<p><u>External Lighting Details</u></p><p>The external lighting shall be installed, operated and maintained strictly in accordance with the Lighting and Light Impact Statement hereby approved and at no time shall the level of illumination exceed 500 lux for the Hockey Pitch and 200 lux for the padel courts.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p><p>REASON:&nbsp;To protect residential amenity, safeguard ecological receptors, and ensure lighting levels remain appropriate for the site in accordance with London Plan Policy G6 and Local Plan policies D12.2, D12.3, O15.1-O15.4.</p>

Urban Greening Factor - The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until the Urban Greening factors set out in the Urban Greening Factor Calculator have been fully implemented and shall be permanently maintained as such thereafter to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: In order to ensure that new development incorporates green infrastructure, to help create healthier places, enhance biodiversity and address the urban heat island effect and to comply with Policy G5 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy O15.5 of the Local Plan 2024.

<p><u>Biodiversity Gain Plan</u></p><p>No development shall commence (excluding site clearance and enabling works) until a Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Biodiversity Gain Plan shall demonstrate how the development will achieve the required 10% Biodiversity Net Gain, and where on‑site measures are insufficient, shall include:</p><p>- Evidence of the purchase and allocation of off‑site BNG units from a legally secured and registered habitat‑bank provider</p><p>- A statement confirming the type, location and habitat classification of the off‑site units</p><p>- Confirmation that the off‑site units are recorded on the BNG Register in accordance with the Environment Act 2021</p><p>- A timetable for delivery and evidence of the minimum 30‑year management and monitoring arrangements</p><p>- A completed Biodiversity Metric calculation demonstrating compliance with the statutory 10% requirement</p><p>The development shall thereafter be carried out in full accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan, and the off‑site units shall be secured for a minimum period of 30 years.</p><p>Reason: To ensure the development delivers the statutory 10% Biodiversity Net Gain in accordance with the Environment Act 2021, the Biodiversity Net Gain Regulations 2024, and relevant London Plan Policy G6 and Merton Local Plan policies O15.1-O15.4.</p>

﻿Hardstanding (Flooding) - The hardstanding hereby permitted shall be made of porous materials, or provision made to direct surface water run-off to a permeable or porous area or surface within the application site before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use.

Reason:  To reduce surface water run-off and to reduce pressure on the surrounding drainage system in accordance with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policy SI12 of the London Plan 2021 and policies F15.7, F15.8 and F15.9 of the Local Plan 2024.

Construction Management Plan/ Dust Management Plan

1.Prior to the commencement of development, including any demolition, a detailed Demolition and Construction Environmental Management Plan (DCEMP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The DCEMP shall include:

(a) An Air quality management plan that identifies the steps and procedures that will be implemented to minimise the creation and impact of dust and other air emissions resulting from the site preparation, demolition, and groundwork and construction phases of the development. An assessment of increased traffic flows (NO2, PM10, PM2.5) from users should be included. If the development causes a significant increase in traffic mitigation is required.

(b) Construction environmental management plan that identifies the steps and procedures that will be implemented to minimise the creation and impact of noise, vibration, dust and other air emissions resulting from the site preparation, demolition, and groundwork and construction phases of the development, including anti idling initiatives.

2. The development shall not be implemented other than in accordance with the approved scheme, unless previously agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.


Reason : To manage and prevent further deterioration of existing low-quality air across London in accordance with London Plan Policies SI1(B)(1c), SI1(B)(2d) and NPPF 199.

Hours of Use - The use hereby permitted shall operate only between the hours of 06.30-22.30 on Mondays - Saturdays and 07.30-18.30 on Sundays and Bank Holidays.

Reason:  To safeguard the amenities of surrounding area and to ensure compliance with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policies D4 and D14 of the London Plan 2021 and policies D12.1 & D12.3 of the Local Plan 2024.

Cycle Parking  - Details to be Submitted - Prior to first use of the development hereby approved, details of 20 x secure cycle parking facilities (incorporating at least 5% of the 20 cycle spaces can accommodate oversized cycles) and a separate cycle/scooter hire bay for the visitors to the development have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 

The approved facilities shall be fully implemented and made available for use prior to the first occupation of the development and thereafter retained for use at all times.

Reason: To ensure satisfactory facilities for cycle parking are provided and to comply with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policy T5 of the London Plan 2021 and policy T16.1 and T16.2 of the Local Plan 2024.

﻿Surface Treatment - Prior to first use of the development hereby approved, details of the surfacing of all those parts of the site not covered by buildings or soft landscaping, including any parking, service areas or roads, footpaths, hard and soft have been submitted in writing for approval by the Local Planning Authority. No works that are the subject of this condition shall be carried out until the details are approved, and the development shall not be occupied / the use of the development hereby approved shall not commence until the details have been approved and works to which this condition relates have been carried out in accordance with the approved details.

Reason:  To ensure a satisfactory standard of development in accordance with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policy D4 of the London Plan 2021 and policies D12.1 and D12.3 of the Local Plan 2024

<p>Noise levels, (expressed as the equivalent continuous sound level) LAeq (1 Hour), from the use associated with the padel courts and hockey pitch shall not exceed 50dB (1 hour) at the boundary with the closest residential property. If it exceeds this level then noise mitigation measures agreed with the Local Planning Authority shall be implemented to control any increase of noise above that predicted in the acoustic report. These mitigation measures shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, in consultation with Environmental Health.</p><p>Reason: In the interests of neighbouring amenity, in accordance with Policy D12.3 of the Local Plan 2024.</p>

<p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;"><u style="">Bat sensitive lighting strategy</u></span></p><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Prior to the installation of the external lighting hereby approved, details of a Bat‑Sensitive Lighting Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The strategy shall be prepared in accordance with <span role="button" tabindex="0" data-url="ca://s?q=Explain_bat_sensitive_lighting_guidance" style="">bat‑sensitive lighting guidance</span> (including ILP/ BCT <em style="">Guidance Note 08/23</em>) and shall include:</span></p><ul role="list"><li><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">A lighting layout plan showing luminaires, lux levels and light‑spill contours</span></p></li><li><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Details of luminaire specifications, mounting heights, shielding, timers and dimming controls</span></p></li><li><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Identification of bat foraging and commuting corridors and measures to maintain them in darkness</span></p></li><li><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Operational controls to ensure lighting is used only when required</span></p></li><li><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">A monitoring and review mechanism to ensure ongoing compliance</span></p></li></ul><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">The development shall thereafter be carried out and operated strictly in accordance with the approved Bat‑Sensitive Lighting Strategy for the lifetime of the development.</span></p><p><span style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Reason: To protect bats and other nocturnal wildlife in accordance with the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981, the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017, and London Plan policy G6 and Merton Local Plan policies O15.1-O15.4</span></p>

Tree Protection (Exclusion Zone) - No demolition or site works shall commence until details of construction exclusion zones to include the protection of the retained trees identified in the Tree Survey Plan have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority and the approved details are fully in place. Any building construction outside of the construction exclusion zone, but within an area identified for root protection, shall be protected using ground protection as detailed in BS 5837:2012, or as required by the Local Planning Authority. The details as approved shall be retained and maintained until the completion of all site operations.

Reason:  To protect and safeguard the existing retained trees in accordance with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policy G7 of the London Plan 2021 and policies O15.1, O15.2 and O15.4 of the Local Plan 2024.

description: Application for the installation of an all-weather sports facilities comprising a synthetic turf hockey pitch with fencing and 6no. floodlight columns, 4no. covered and floodlit padel courts, provision of 3no. artificial cricket wickets and a no-dig woodland path.
